title: Opposition and Coalition Position Ahead of Kast's First Cuenta Pública to Congress on June 1
detail: On the eve of President José Antonio Kast's first Cuenta Pública (annual State of the Union) to a joint session of Congress in Valparaíso on June 1, Chile's political factions publicly staked out positions for and against the government's first 82 days in office. The governing Partido Republicano and Chile Vamos allies anticipated flagship announcements on the 7-axis security plan, migration enforcement results, and the path of the economic reactivation mega-bill (already passed the Chamber 90-59-1) through the Senate. The center-left and left opposition — including Partido Comunista, Frente Amplio (ex-Boric coalition), and Partido Socialista — coordinated a unified response condemning the May 19 cabinet reshuffle, rising fuel costs (whose planned tax hike Kast ultimately reversed), escalating Army-Carabineros operations at Temucuicui, and the Q1 2026 GDP contraction of 0.5% YoY. With approval at 26-39% depending on the polling firm (Data Influye vs. Cadem), the Cuenta Pública was Kast's most consequential communication opportunity since his March 11 inauguration.

title: Cochilco Raises 2026 Copper Price Forecast to $5.55/lb as Metal Hits Record $6.39/lb on LME
detail: Chile's national copper commission COCHILCO revised its 2026 annual average copper price forecast sharply upward — from US$4.95 per pound to US$5.55 per pound — citing surging global demand driven by electrification, AI data center infrastructure, and the green energy transition. Copper prices briefly reached a 2026 record of US$6.39 per pound on the London Metal Exchange, representing a 38%+ annual gain and the highest nominal copper price in history. COCHILCO simultaneously revised Chile's 2026 production forecast slightly downward by approximately 2%, to 5.3 million metric tonnes, citing operational disruptions at some mines despite Codelco posting 3.7% YoY output growth in its Q1 2026 report. The price surge significantly improves Chile's fiscal outlook, given copper represents approximately 50% of total export revenues and CODELCO remains a major source of direct transfers to the state budget. Chile's lithium exports also rose sharply: Q1 2026 revenues reached $1.108 billion, up 147.7% YoY.
